pages.title: A phone inside the story
paragraphs: Give players a phone they can open in chat: installed apps, changing shortcuts, an App Store, nested business lists and narrator-generated service pages. A restaurant can lead to its menu, a job board to an offer, and a contact app to a conversation while the surrounding game continues.

Scripts own the installed-app list, shortcuts, selected app, configured directory entries, discovery filters, layout preference and reveal flags. The narrator presents those screens and generates page contents. The host game owns purchases, items, messages, appointments, contracts, quests and their consequences.

This is a single-player narrative interface. It is not a separate web app, a fixed-width phone image, a transaction engine or an authoritative alarm scheduler. The current adapter leaves phone state unchanged when it cannot identify exactly one player.
New in 0.7.0: discuss and approve custom skills or abilities, then practice them through ordinary gameplay. The example profile provides a Workshop app; creators can place these pages in another app.
table: Open the app currently assigned D, from Home
Browse a configured page or contextual detail
pages.note: Suggested first test: phone → phone store → phone open Maps → phone view nearby. Ordinary narration and the host clock continue; browsing can consume story time.

pages.title: Install as a Voyage mod
pages.lead: Use the complete native mod file. No local merger or Node installation is needed.
paragraphs: 1. Export a complete backup of your world. Make a named test copy before adding TextPhone. Use only the customized profile for Your Power Is What; adapt the generic profile for other worlds.
2. Open Voyage Creator Studio. In the content chooser, select Mods, then Create Mod. Open Publish, give it a clear name and use Save mod. Keep it Private while preparing it.

3. Open the supplied build/generic-phone-voyage-mod.json in a text editor and copy all of it. This is the complete mod draft; the smaller *-phone-mod.json in the source repository is a build input, not a whole editor replacement.
4. In the new mod's Studio, select Content and the top-level Content entry. Use View JSON if needed. Replace the entire initial GameState editor with the complete mod draft and select Save mod.
5. Reload the mod and confirm its content saved. Open your test world's Studio > Mods. Under My mods, choose Add draft for this TextPhone mod, then select Apply.
6. Reload the world and check its content before starting a fresh test game. Open phone, its App Store and the workshop choices. Keep your original export for rollback.
pages.note: For a world you intend to publish, Voyage requires attached mods to be published too. Complete your mod's rating and publishing controls before publishing the world. Do not attach both generic and customized TextPhone.

pages.title: Native compatibility and edited worlds
pages.lead: Check both the installed interface and the host rules it uses.
paragraphs: TextPhone adds phone_mod_ records and four AI instruction entries. Existing world content should remain intact. In AI > Story, keep the world's existing sections alongside TextPhone Interface and TextPhone Workshops.

In AI > Advanced > Action Info and Learned Abilities, inspect custom instructions after Apply. If you already use those fields, preserve your guidance and include the TextPhone Workshops block once. Local edits and other mods can affect which version survives; the offline installer can combine these blocks and report conflicts.

A source-linked remix can reapply inherited world data when mods are applied. If unrelated music, image settings or world guidance changes, restore your backup and use a fresh standalone world containing your complete exported content. Detach only the inherited source-world mod reference in that standalone copy; retain any real dependencies your world needs.

The complete native mod draft carries required Voyage defaults so Studio can save it. It is a mod definition for a new Mod, not a replacement for your populated world. Use the complete-world installer when you need explicit field-preserving reconciliation.
pages.note: Installation in a standalone Your Power Is What copy is supported. Arbitrary mod stacks, multiplayer and existing-save migration require their own compatibility checks.

pages.title: Workshop a skill or ability
pages.lead: Discuss a design, approve it, then practice it in the story.
paragraphs: 1. Open the phone and its workshop app. Choose Ability creation for a new purchasable power, Skill creation for a trainable skill, or Technique creation for an application of an existing power.
2. Describe what you want it to do, its theme, scope and limits. Discuss changes in chat. The workshop keeps the discussion on the phone at your current location.
3. Review the complete proposal: Name, Effect, Limits, Costs and Practice. Abilities and techniques also include a Native card: the concise description proposed for the purchase screen.
4. Enter the exact phone confirm command shown for the latest draft. This saves that revision as an approved design. A design is not yet a learned skill or purchased ability.

5. Enter practice skill [name] or practice ability [name], replacing [name] with the approved name. Technique practice uses practice ability. This closes the design interface and requests an ordinary exercise in the world.

6. Practice again when appropriate. Accept an actual native skill offer with Learn, or review a native ability offer and purchase it through the normal ability controls. Check the offered description before buying.
pages.note: Workshop guidance keeps narration focused on design, but cannot pause the whole engine. Ticks, time, resources and native events may still advance. Use it outside urgent scenes.

pages.title: Practice and native acquisition
pages.lead: Voyage owns learning eligibility, offers and purchase costs.
paragraphs: There is no guaranteed number of practice attempts. A well-defined approved design gives the narrator and native generation systems a consistent target; it does not force a grant or change the world learning probabilities.

An ability offer is a candidate for normal purchase. Available points, prerequisites and other native rules still apply. The proposed Native card helps carry the agreed meaning forward, but the generated offer can summarize or change it.

A skill offer uses Voyage's native Learn interaction. The resulting character skill may store its name and governing attribute without the full workshop description. TextPhone retains the approved scope separately and supplies it when that skill is named in an ordinary action.

Narration saying that something was learned is not the native offer. Check the real offer or Character panel. If no offer appears, improve the exercise or continue appropriate practice; do not assume the mod promises an unlock.

Use phone workshop cancel to close an unfinished discussion. The currently saved approved design remains available for practice. A newer workshop replaces the active session; the player's previously acquired native abilities and skills remain owned by Voyage.
pages.note: The phone supports one current workshop per identified single player. Keep a separate note if you want an archive of older design specifications.

pages.title: Add workshop pages to an app
pages.lead: Use any suitable app; Pulse is only the customized placement.
paragraphs: Add a workshop page to an enabled app's pages array. Use distinct names so Ability creation and Skill creation remain separate choices. The app must be installed before its pages can be opened.

workshopKind is ability, skill or technique. guidance describes that page's world-specific expectations: power theme, learning constraints or what existing power a technique should extend. Keep host mechanics authoritative.

Rebuild the mod and install the resulting version using the installation or upgrade steps. Removing all workshop pages omits the workshop handlers and their instruction blocks. Setting an app's enabled field to false disables that app.
pages.note: Each app allows up to 12 pages. Workshop pages open with phone view PAGE; they are not startsActivity pages.

pages.title: Workshop API and integration
pages.lead: Versioned consent state, captured model output and native handoff.
table: storage.phone_mod.players[JSON.stringify(playerName)].workshop; schemaVersion 1, owner, kind, sequence, revision and status.
drafting → review → requested → closed. requested means an approved design, not native acquisition.
name (80), effect (1200), limits (1000), costs (600), practice (600); nativeCard (1200) for new ability/technique sessions. Limits are TextPhone characters, not native engine limits.
approved contains requestId, owner, kind, sequence, revision and the full draft. Confirmation requires the current sequence.revision; duplicate confirmation creates no new request.

A complete TEXTPHONE DRAFT sequence.revision block through END DRAFT. Ordered unique fields are required. Defined bold labels and hyphen/en-dash/em-dash separators are accepted; field values remain intact.
Story: TextPhone Interface and TextPhone Workshops sections. Action Info and Learned Abilities: delimited TextPhone Workshops blocks in custom.
Scripts emit context and retain the approved design. They do not call an ability/skill generator, grant points, force a native offer or directly purchase the result.
pages.note: Keep the metadata, capture and planning handlers together. Editing only displayed draft text does not update the saved approval.

pages.title: Customize and rebuild
pages.lead: Optional: edit apps and rebuild with Node.js 20 or newer.
paragraphs: 1. Download the full generic source from github.com/Morberis/textphone-for-voyage using Code > Download ZIP. Extract it on your computer. Node.js 20 or newer is required for rebuilding.
2. Copy config/generic-phone.json from this creator package into the source project's config folder. Open that file in a text editor. The following pages explain app settings, examples and APIs.
3. Make your changes and save the configuration. Keep app IDs stable, use exact world location IDs, and give new apps distinct IDs and labels.
4. Open a terminal in the source folder containing package.json. Run the three commands below, entering each command on ONE line. No npm install or API key is needed.

5. Build a complete native mod draft with the third command, then use that file in your mod's Studio Content editor. The HTML installer remains available for combining edited host guidance or installing directly into a full world export.
pages.code:
node native/build-mod.mjs config/generic-phone.json build/mod.json

node native/build-installer.mjs build/mod.json build/install.html

node native/build-draft.mjs build/mod.json build/voyage-mod.json
pages.note: Run each displayed command as one line. The outputs are build/mod.json (partial build), build/install.html (local world installer), and build/voyage-mod.json (complete native Mod draft). Generated files are replaced when you rebuild.

pages.title: Merge your world export
pages.lead: Fallback or upgrade reconciliation: combine your complete world with TextPhone locally.
paragraphs: 1. Extract the creator ZIP on your computer. Open its textphone-for-voyage folder. You should see the build folder inside it.
2. In Voyage, make a test copy using More > Remix on the source world, or More > Duplicate on your own world. Give the copy a TEST__ name and confirm you are editing that copy.
3. In the test copy's Studio, select Content, then the top-level Content entry in the left tree. The breadcrumb should read Content. Select View JSON if the editor shows a form.
4. Select Download initial GameState JSON above the editor. Keep this complete export unchanged as your backup. It must be the whole world, not a running save or just the Triggers section.
5. On your computer, open build/generic-phone-installer.html from the extracted package in your browser.
6. Under Original world JSON, choose the complete export saved in step 4.
7. Select Prepare updated world. Review the result and record counts. If an error appears, stop here and resolve it; do not install a partial result.
8. Select Download updated world JSON. Keep this new file separate from your original backup. This is the complete world with TextPhone added.
Next: follow Add the result in Voyage on the next page, using the NEW file from step 8. The merge has not yet changed your live world.
pages.note: The merger updates phone_mod_ triggers and adds the narrator bridge while retaining other world fields. A different existing phone bridge requires review. Use only one phone profile per world.

pages.title: Add the result in Voyage
pages.lead: Install the complete merged definition into the identified test copy.
paragraphs: 1. Open with-phone.json in a text editor and copy its entire contents. For the browser route, use Copy complete JSON or open the downloaded file. Do not copy the partial build/*-phone-mod.json: it contains only phone records and integration instructions.

2. Return to that test copy in Voyage Studio. Select Content, then the top-level Content entry so the breadcrumb is just Content. Choose View JSON if the editor is in form mode. Confirm you are in the complete initial GameState editor, not a single trigger or a running save editor.

3. Click inside the JSON text, press Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on macOS) while that editor is focused, and paste the complete prepared JSON. Use Save in the Studio toolbar. This is an editor replacement using the merged complete file, not a file upload or a Mods > Apply step.

4. Reload Studio and download the saved complete world again. Compare it with your prepared file before playtesting. With the source project, use the command below; without it, use a JSON-aware comparison tool. Review any differences before continuing.

5. Start a fresh game from the test world. Name and record the save as a test where the interface allows it. Send phone, then phone store, then a shortcut actually displayed on Home. Open each configured app, test its directory and toggles, and continue ordinary play. Check stored state as well as the narrator’s description of consequences.
Existing saves are not automatically updated. Use the supplied merger for this release. Purchases, payments and messages remain the responsibility of the world and narrator.
pages.note: Enter the comparison command on ONE line. Without Node, compare the prepared and saved complete JSON in a JSON-aware diff tool; counts alone cannot establish full equality.

pages.title: Upgrade an existing TextPhone world
pages.lead: Keep your app configuration and original export before changing versions.
paragraphs: 1. Export the complete current world and preserve its existing mod version. Keep your edited app configuration separately; an upgrade must not silently restore example apps or erase creator choices.
2. Copy your configuration into the new source release. Add the desired workshop pages and rebuild, or use the supplied customized profile if you have not changed its settings.

3. For a native installation, update your existing TextPhone mod draft with the new complete Voyage mod JSON, save it, then open the test world's Mods page and select Apply. Keep only one TextPhone profile attached.

4. Reload and export the test world. Check the phone records and AI > Story plus AI > Advanced > Action Info and Learned Abilities. Preserve your own guidance. If local edits prevent the new blocks from appearing, use the included installer on the backed-up complete world export to reconcile owned blocks; follow the numbered merge steps.

5. Open a fresh test game and check Home, App Store and the new workshop choices. Verify your enabled apps, discovery and delivery settings. Existing saves may keep an earlier script snapshot; changing the world does not prove a running save was upgraded.
6. Keep the previous mod/export until your new version works. Restore that known-good version if needed. Do not delete an existing save or reset learned skills just to update phone code.
pages.note: 0.7.0 retains phone storage schema 1. New ability and technique drafts include a Native card; earlier approvals can use their full saved description. The standalone world installer replaces owned blocks and refuses ambiguous edited blocks or oversized combined instructions.

pages.title: Existing saves and rollback
pages.lead: World installation and saved-game migration are different operations.
paragraphs: A fresh game uses the updated world definition. A running game also carries its own generated content, character state and phone state. Treat it as unchanged until you verify the new behavior there; the local installer does not edit running saves.

This package has no automatic saved-game migrator. Do not paste a world export into a game State Editor or clear phone_mod storage to force an upgrade. A save-specific migration must preserve characters, purchases, installed and revealed apps, shortcuts and host-system state.

To undo a world upgrade: open the affected world in Studio, select the top-level Content entry, choose View JSON, replace the editor contents with the complete backup from before the upgrade, then Save and reload. Read back the saved export and compare it with that backup.
Restoring a world definition does not undo actions already taken in a running game. Retain the prior package, edited configuration and pre-upgrade world export until you no longer need rollback.

When requesting help, include the old and new TextPhone versions, profile, the failed step and the exact error. State whether the problem occurs in a fresh game or an existing save. Share only the relevant configuration or instruction section rather than a complete private save.

pages.title: Choose the settings that matter
paragraphs: Edit config/generic-phone.json, then rebuild. The starting apps are Messages, Maps, Food Delivery and App Store. Clock is configured but disabled; creators can enable it after connecting a suitable time system. Corner Cafe is an example: replace its catalogue entry with a business from your own world.
table: Default Home layout for a new phone: false=single, true=paired. Existing players keep their stored choice.
Per app: false omits it from the built mod; true or omitted enables it. Includes App Store.
Enabled app IDs installed on a new phone. Include App Store when enabled.
The app that opens the scripted download catalogue.
Per app: public, or triggered until revealed. This is separate from business discovery.
Per app: false protects it from uninstall. App Store is always protected.
Per app: known, all_public, or curated.
Per app: exact location/area exclusions and optional messages.
Optional name of a compact public clock record in host script storage.
paragraphs_after: Use stable IDs when renaming labels. The app label is what players type; the ID owns saved installation state. Reordering the catalogue does not intentionally reassign an existing valid shortcut. A removed configuration ID is pruned from that player’s phone the next time it is processed.
pages.note: Known means the world regards a named entity as known; it does not mean visited. The current native adapter rejects the visited listing mode. Device possession is not required and no invented device-availability flag is used.

pages.title: Turn any app on or off
paragraphs: Every app, including App Store, supports enabled:true or enabled:false. Omitted means true for older configurations. Disabled apps are excluded during the build: their app instructions and business data are not shipped. A story reveal cannot enable an excluded app.

Use enabled:false to turn an app off. Use enabled:true with triggered visibility for an app that should exist but remain hidden until an event. Starting installation and player uninstall protection remain independent.
Disabling App Store removes its Home control and disables install/remove commands. Other preinstalled enabled apps still work. The Store must be in initialInstalledIds when enabled.

Rebuild both generated files, merge into a test world and start a fresh save. Existing world saves are not automatically updated. After an explicit script update, removed IDs are pruned at the next phone request; re-enabling does not reinstall them in that existing registry.
table: enabled:true; visibility public; omit initial ID
enabled:true; visibility triggered; omit initial ID
Starts off. Enable after connecting a suitable host time system.
pages.note: The switch controls this module. Independent world lore and narration may still mention the service. Do not treat it as a guaranteed narrative ban.

pages.title: Add a custom app
paragraphs: Add an object to the apps array with a unique id, label and order. This example adds a transit app that can be downloaded. To preinstall it in a new game, also add transit to initialInstalledIds.
paragraphs_after: Generated pages use phone view routes. An activity page uses phone choose request ticket. Opening the app itself does not select the activity.

The short summary appears in the Store and opening menu. Give it a concrete purpose: a name alone can lead the narrator to invent the wrong kind of service. Put general service rules in app.guidance and page-specific work in page.guidance. Keep the host’s existing rules in force.
pages.note: Use examples/transit-app.json for copying. To continue inside a generated menu, the player can use ordinary language. A generated phone view detail also retains the current app context, but it is model-mediated browsing rather than a new deterministic transaction command.

pages.title: Business lists and generated menus
paragraphs: A directory is a curated set of candidate businesses attached to one app. All public means all entries marked public in that configured set; it does not scan every store in the world. The same world location can participate in several apps with different policies.
table: Public entries whose exact locationId passes known-entity
Every public entry in this app’s configured catalogue
Public entries also listed in directory.curatedIds
paragraphs_after: For a curated list, add "curatedIds": ["corner-cafe"]. Set public:false to exclude a candidate from every listing mode. Add a page with kind:directory and optionally use openPage to open it immediately.

The listed number selects that business. The narrator then generates offerings and indicative prices. Numbers inside that generated menu are interpreted by narration and do not select another business. Back returns from menu to list, then from list to Home.
pages.note: Descriptions are catalogue data. Explain what the business sells; do not hide engine instructions in them. Generated offerings and prices are not cached by this module. Use examples/store-app.json.

pages.title: Delivery rules belong to each app
paragraphs: Configure exclusions independently for each app. An area-specific message takes precedence over a whole-location rule; otherwise the app message is used. Location and area IDs must match the host’s native values exactly.
paragraphs_after: phone delivery check tests the player’s current location and area in the currently open delivery app. It reports an exclusion, a missing destination, or that the destination is not excluded. The check does not place a new order.

Not excluded is narrower than available: opening hours, stock, service coverage, funds, weather, fees and arrival estimates still belong to the host service. Natural-language ordering receives the app’s exclusions as context. An alternative destination must be checked under those same rules.

This module can deterministically select and emit the refusal message. It cannot guarantee that every host model will obey it or veto every native purchase writer. Treat it as an integration policy, not an atomic financial guard.
pages.note: There is no shared global blacklist. Giving Food Delivery a blocked location does not block a shopping app. Use examples/store-app.json for a complete editable app; configure both apps separately if both should be restricted.

pages.title: Hidden apps and real unlock triggers
paragraphs: For an enabled app, set appStoreVisibility:triggered and leave it out of initialInstalledIds. The scripted catalogue omits it and the registry rejects a premature installation request. Live narration can still invent a successful installation: this is visibility/state control, not a guaranteed prose restriction. A reveal makes it available; it does not install it or grant account access.
paragraphs_after: Place that script in a creator-authored trigger with the actual quest, event or other supported condition that should reveal the app. The ID signal_vault must equal your app ID. Use the existing player key exactly; it includes JSON string quoting.

Alternatively, set unlockKnownEntity to an exact host entity name. A true known-entity result reveals the app when its phone is next processed. Reveal is persistent in this release; turning a grant back to false does not revoke a reveal that was already recorded.

Public download visibility, installed state and service authorization are separate. A public job app can still require membership before accepting work. Use app/page guidance to connect that service to the world’s existing access rules.
pages.note: examples/hidden-app.json and examples/reveal-trigger.json provide complete records. Replace the example quest condition with your world’s real trigger. The adapter currently requires exactly one player; this example is not multiplayer attribution.

pages.title: Connect the host systems
table: Exactly one action string and one key from check(player-level); state is keyed by JSON.stringify(player name).
check(party-location) and check(party-area); used by Maps and delivery checks.
check(known-entity) for each configured exact locationId. No native historical-visit reader.
Disabled by default. Scripts cannot read the built-in clock. Optional clockStorageKey reads a creator-provided custom storage record for Time page context.
Host-generated transaction and state systems; the phone does not charge, pay or maintain a second ledger.
Host story/state systems; existing relationships, access rules and explicit choices remain relevant.
May supply time and continuity through the host. The generic phone has no required LC dependency.
paragraphs_after: To enable Clock, find app id clock in your profile config and set enabled:true. Its supplied public visibility then allows downloading. Add clock to initialInstalledIds only if it should start installed in new games. Rebuild the mod and installer. LC installation alone does not configure the connection.

For an optional clock adapter, write a small public record such as storage.public_clock = {date:"2040-05-03", time:"09:20"}, then set clockStorageKey:"public_clock". Keep that record short: at most 1000 serialized characters are included. The host adapter must update it before the relevant phone turn; this module does not infer a civil date from game-tick.

Clock Alarms is a generated view, not a new scheduler. If your world requires dependable alarms, connect an existing authoritative event system and verify both the stored event and its later firing. An attractive generated alarm list is insufficient evidence.

To advance to a specific time, enter Advance time to [time] in the normal story input, replacing [time] with your target time. To wait a duration, enter Wait [number] hours, replacing [number] with the hours to pass. The Clock Time page displays these instructions. The host handles time passage and intervening events.
pages.note: There is no inventory-based device gate. Renaming a player can create a different phone key. Multiplayer is unsupported.

pages.title: Code and integration points
table: Validate configuration and build inert data records plus six native handlers. Returns {triggers}.
Return a separate complete world and preservation report; reject saves and conflicting bridges.
Read configuration, attribute the player, restore/prune phone state, allocate stable shortcuts and build screen context.
Home, layout, close/back, install, uninstall and hidden download visibility.
Configured pages, activity choice, directory selection and generated-menu context.
Per-app policy checks and context for natural or generated detail requests.
Versioned design, captured proposal, explicit approval, typed practice and learned-skill context.
paragraphs_after: The builder emits phone_mod_config_* and phone_mod_data_* records as JSON inside inert script comments, read with JSON.parse. Runtime triggers use action-text conditions, planning phase and party scope. They use the documented storage, triggers, check, effects and log surfaces; they do not evaluate generated code.

Only edit readable source/configuration, then rebuild. Deployment scripts remove indentation/comments to fit native limits; complete world exports stay pretty-printed. In Studio the generated records are under Content → Mechanics → Advanced → Triggers.
pages.note: These source files are in the generic GitHub project. The creator package contains your editable profile and the already-built installer.

pages.title: API and persistence reference
table: Case-insensitive exact app label; updates installation revision. Existing host orders/accounts are not deleted by script.
Browse a configured page. An unregistered detail continues inside the current app as model-mediated browsing.
Invoke a configured startsActivity:true page; ordinary page viewing does not invoke it.
Open the current app’s eligible business list / select an exact listed label. phone restaurant NAME is an alias.
Scripted directory menu→list→Home; from other app pages returns Home. Generated labels may claim a different destination.
Installed/revealed IDs, shortcuts, layout, app/page/directory, revision and lastHandled receipt.
Creator grant:true reveals the download on the next processed phone action.
paragraphs_after: The receipt combines game tick and action text to prevent duplicate scripted navigation effects across handlers. A generated detail adds context without inventing a deterministic transaction. Natural conversation does not silently navigate the phone.

Configuration bounds: 32 apps, 12 pages per app, 128 businesses per app, unique lowercase ASCII app IDs up to 48 characters, unique short app labels up to 32 characters, and one-line summaries up to 160 characters. Page names use letters, spaces and hyphens, up to 40 characters. App/page guidance is bounded to 1800 characters each. Commands are limited to 400 characters. The builder also rejects any serialized trigger above 10000 characters.

Changing the starting app list or default layout affects new phone state. Existing state retains its installed IDs and chosen layout, apart from IDs removed from the current catalogue. Start a fresh game when changing profiles; legacy save migration is not provided.
pages.note: Do not install two phone profiles together under the same namespace. Use the complete-profile merger to remove obsolete phone records. Keep unrelated trigger names outside phone_mod_. Workshop state and commands are documented in Workshop API and integration.

pages.title: Check your installation and troubleshoot
paragraphs: 1. Start a fresh game. Enter phone, open an app using its displayed shortcut, then try phone store. Close and reopen the save to check that installed apps and preferences persist.

2. Check that the world's original NPCs, locations, quests and lore are still present. After configuration changes, check both sides of the options you changed, such as allowed/blocked delivery or before/after a hidden-app reveal.
3. For purchases and other important actions, check the game's actual inventory, currency or quest state. A narrated success is not always a recorded result.
table: Narrator omits or changes a screen
Try an exact app command and inspect state. Home can repeat a prior invented app, so returning Home is not a guaranteed recovery.
Use ordinary-language follow-up. phone view details has contextual routing; other invented commands are not guaranteed.
Use clear word-bearing rows and explicitly confirm the quoted total. Inspect native consequences.
Connect authoritative host records if required; generated prose alone is not a stored fact.
Do not advertise support with this adapter.
Use the verified complete-export merge route until Mods → Apply is separately checked.
pages.note: Use a test copy and keep the original export. Existing saves are not automatically upgraded; multiplayer is unsupported. Normal narration continues and browsing may advance story time.

pages.title: Optional improvements and sources
paragraphs: Creators can extend the phone without adding a new engine for every app. Start with a short purpose and one useful page, then add only the host connections the experience requires.
bullets: Author a merchant catalogue per service, including location IDs, useful descriptions and discovery policy.
Add a transit, journal, club, guild, weather, medical appointment or property app using generated pages and existing host systems.
Reveal an app through a quest, invitation or known place; keep download visibility separate from account permission.
Add an authoritative menu/cart/order or alarm adapter if exact persistence matters. This is extra implementation, not an undocumented built-in feature.
Provide explicit profile candidates or service eligibility data where broad narrator guidance is too variable.
Choose the starting apps and delivery messages that suit each world. A smaller catalogue usually makes the first phone interaction easier to read.
pages.note: TextPhone is independently authored and is not an official Latitude feature. MIT covers its original code and documentation; third-party world material remains separate.

pages.title: Creator installation checklist
paragraphs: Check these steps on your own test remix. Checkmarks record your review, not a guarantee of model behavior.
checklist: Preserve the original complete world export and identify a test copy.
Choose one phone profile; preserve your app IDs and creator configuration.
Set enabled apps, starting downloads, discovery and delivery policies.
Install the complete native Mod draft into a Mod, then Add draft and Apply to the world; or use the complete-world installer.
Reload and verify the installed version, phone records and AI guidance.
Confirm original lore, NPCs, locations, quests and host rules remain.
Start a fresh test game and check Home, App Store and configured pages.
Check separate Ability creation and Skill creation choices.
Review a complete proposal and confirm only its current revision.
Check reveal, installation, shortcuts and save/reload behavior.
Review the gameplay limits and native offer before sharing or purchase.
For an upgrade, retain the previous mod and export until the new version is accepted.
